articles.title: Central bank bonanza in Scandinavia
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
There were large movements in the financial markets yesterday, and once again statistics from the US show unexpected resilience and strength despite obvious growth risks linked to the Middle East. Yesterday's message of strength came from the PMI, where manufacturing but especially the service sector surprised with further gains. If you disregard the large movements during the pandemic, we have to go back to 2015 before we find correspondingly high PMI figures, even the euro area showed surprisingly strong PMI numbers The combination of a continued strong economy together with high energy prices lifts expectations of policy rate hikes further and US Treasury yields rose by 15 basis points, both the 2- and 10-year. Weak demand for an auction and Fed statements about the need for more rate hikes also contributed to rising yields. The US 10-year yield is now trading around 5.11%. European yields followed suit but the increase stayed just below 10 basis points. The rise in yields turned the stock markets downwards and the US indices fell around 1 percent. The decline in Europe was lower, but stock market futures point to a continued decline today. Stock markets in Asia are also falling except in Tokyo, where the Nikkei is up by over 1%.
Export ban on diesel remains on the agenda
. The resilience of the real economy lifted oil prices yesterday, but reports of successful transports through the Strait of Hormuz have reversed the trend overnight. Worse still, discussions about a US export ban on diesel seem to be continuing. Yesterday, diesel futures in the US fell on the data, while the corresponding figure in Europe rose sharply. The oil industry gives the thumbs down, and also points out that it could have the effect of making petrol more expensive. However, nothing has been decided.
Today's agenda is packed
 with central bank decisions and surveys on the state of the economy. Eyes are also turned to New York and the UN annual meeting, where Trump has now given Xi a tarmac welcomed. At the same time, Finance Minister Bessent announced a two-month extension of the "trade peace" with China.
Norges Bank is raising interest rates, but there is considerable uncertainty.
 Norges Bank has previously indicated a need for higher interest rates, but more favourable inflation outcomes have raised questions about whether the need really exists. We expect it to still fall into a hike and that the interest rate path will continue to indicate a hike going forward, but we also note that expectations for the day are split and see the decision as 50/50, see preview 
here
.
Nordic key stories
Unchanged from the Riksbank, but guidance going forward is super important.
 We expect the Riksbank to keep the policy rate unchanged today, but that the inflation risk still means that the interest rate path indicates a 60% probability of a hike in the next three meetings. The good starting point means that the Riksbank has the opportunity to take more information into account, but developments in recent weeks have contributed to a policy rate hike creeping closer. Both the monetary policy report, but above all the press conference, will be extremely important to scrutinize. See the preview 
here
, the investor survey 
here
 and the trader floor survey 
here
.

articles.title: Centralbanksfest i Skandinavien
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Det var stora rörelser på finansmarknaderna igår. Återigen visar statistik från USA en oväntad motståndskraft och styrka trots uppenbara tillväxtrisker kopplade till Mellanöstern. Gårdagens styrkebesked kom från PMI där industrin men framför allt tjänstesektorn överraskade med ytterligare uppgång. Om man bortser från de stora rörelserna under pandemin får vi backa tillbaka till 2015 innan vi hittar motsvarande höga PMI-siffror, även Euroområdet visade på överraskande starka PMI-siffror Kombinationen av fortsatt stark ekonomi tillsammans med höga energipriser lyfter förväntningarna på räntehöjningar ytterligare och amerikanska statsräntor steg med 15 räntepunkter, både 2- och 10-åringen. Svag efterfrågan vid en emission och Fed-uttalanden om behov av fler räntehöjningar bidrog också till räntelyftet. Den amerikanska 10-årsräntan handlas nu kring 5,11%. Europeiska räntor följde efter men uppgången stannade strax under 10 räntepunkter. Ränteuppgången vände börserna nedåt och de amerikanska indexen backade omkring 1 procent. Nedgången i Europa var lägre, men börsterminer pekar mot fortsatt nedgång idag. Börserna i Asien backar också förutom i Tokyo där Nikkei stiger med över 1%.
Exportförbud på diesel fortsatt på agendan
. Realekonomins motståndskraft lyfte igår oljepriset, men uppgifter om lyckade transporter genom Hormuzsundet har vänt utvecklingen under natten. Värre är att diskussionerna om ett amerikanskt exportförbud på diesel verkar fortsätta. Igår föll dieselterminer i USA på uppgifterna, medan motsvarande i Europa steg kraftigt. Oljeindustrin ger tummen ner, och påpekar också att det kan få effekten att bensinen blir dyrare. Inget är dock beslutat.
Dagens agenda är fullmatad
 med centralbanksbeslut och enkätundersökningar om läget i ekonomin. Blickar vänds också mot New York och FN:s årsmöte där Trump nu välkomnat Xi redan vid flygplanet. Finansminister Bessent meddelade samtidigt en två månaders förlängning av ”handelsfreden” med Kina.
Norges bank höjer räntan, men osäkerheten är stor.
 Norges Bank har tidigare indikerat behov av högre ränta, men mer fördelaktiga inflationsutfall har rest frågor om verkligen behovet föreligger. Vi räknar med att det ändå trillar över i en höjning och att räntebanan fortsätter indikera höjning framöver, men vi noterar också att förväntningarna inför dagen är delade och ser beslutet som 50/50, se preview 
här
.
Sverige
Oförändrat från Riksbanken, men guidning framåt superviktig.
 Vi räknar med att Riksbanken håller styrräntan oförändrad idag, men att inflationsrisken ändå gör att räntebanan indikerar 60% sannolikhet för höjning kommande tre möten. Det goda utgångsläget gör att Riksbanken har möjlighet att ta in mer information, men utvecklingen de senaste veckorna har bidragit till att en räntehöjning krupit närmre. Både penningpolitiska rapporten, men framför allt presskonferensen blir ytterst viktig att skärskåda. Se preview 
här
, investerarenkät 
här
 och handlargolvenkät 
här

En vecka kvar till punktskattehöjning.
 Det är idag en vecka kvar innan den första tillfällig sänkningen av energiskatten på drivmedel går ut, med ca 1 kr/liter upp för bensinen. Den större sänkningen av koldioxidskatten försvinner om två månader vilket när det inträffar lyfter priserna på bensin och diesel med ytterligare 3 kr vardera, se diagram nedan.

articles.title: Slightly cheaper oil and waiting for Xi and Trump's meeting
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Oil prices fell yesterday to below $100/barrel 
after Iran said it could open the Strait of Hormuz to traffic "within a week" if the US lifts the blockade, the announcement that Saudi Arabia is about to restart its East-West pipeline and Trump's statements that a US delegation had a three-hour long and "very good" meeting with Iran. In his speech to the UN General Assembly, Trump warned of total annihilation of Iran if the country does not make a deal with the United States, but at the same time said that such an agreement could be delayed until after the US midterm elections, which does not point to any immediate escalation. 
Yesterday, Trump also signed an agreement
 on an increased military presence in Greenland and met with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy to discuss a possible agreement between Ukraine and Russia to stop attacking each other's energy facilities. The world is now looking forward to the next global highlight; the summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi tomorrow, Thursday. The meeting is not expected to lead to a breakthrough in the trade conflict; China's threat to restrict exports of critical minerals gives it a strong negotiating position and limits the scope for the US to push for concessions via tariffs. The fact that Xi is not expected to be accompanied by a large business delegation makes it less likely that the countries would announce new major business deals. Otherwise, discussions on AI are expected to be high on the agenda. 
Record-high diesel 
prices have prompted US Treasury Secretary Bessent and Trump to open the door to a possible export ban. The US currently has a surplus of diesel, but the oil industry warns that this will stop if the administration completely or partially stops the ability to sell to the rest of the world, which would mean only a temporary price relief in the US but further upside pressure in the rest of the world. 
The Nasdaq put the recent AI worries behind it
 with a new price record for the first time since June, while broad US indices fell slightly. The Stockholm stock exchange rose while the krona – after a volatile day – cautiously strengthened against the euro. Norwegian equities followed the oil prices lower while the EUR/NOK traded higher. Asian stock markets are mixed; up in Korea but down in China. Japan remains closed for holidays. US and European stock market futures are rising slightly. 
The September PMI will be the highlight of the day.
 The business sector has been unexpectedly resilient to the conflict in the Middle East, and composite indices for industry and services are at expansionary levels in both the euro area and the US. The question is what effects the renewed rise in energy prices in recent weeks will have on sentiment and prices. The OECD will release an economic update at 10:00 a.m. Norwegian unemployment will be the last piece of data ahead of tomorrow's unusually uncertain rate decision by Norges Bank.
Recommended reading: SEB's revised policy rate forecasts. 
We summarize SEB's views on central banks, long-term interest rates and currencies after the recent rise in energy prices and the increased concern about more persistent inflationary effects. Read more 
here
.
Nordic key stories
SEB's Trading Room survey: The vast majority believe that the Riksbank will leave the interest rate unchanged at 1.75% tomorrow
, but a majority believe in at least one hike before the end of the year. However, market reactions are expected to be surprisingly small, regardless of whether the Riksbank chooses to be clearly hawkish and signal at least one hike until the end of the year, or whether it chooses to signal a 60 per cent probability of a hike over the next three meetings, in line with SEB's main scenario. The latter would mean that the repo rate path ends up far below prevailing market pricing, which currently indicates that the policy rate will be 2.08 per cent in December. Read more 
here
.

articles.title: Något billigare olja och väntan på Xi och Trumps möte
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Oljepriset sjönk under gårdagen till under $100/fatet 
efter att Iran sa att man skulle kunna öppna Hormuz-sundet för trafik ”inom en vecka” om USA lyfter blockaden, beskedet att Saudiarabien är på väg att återstarta sin öst-västliga pipeline samt Trumps uttalanden om att en amerikansk delegation hade ett tre timmar långt och ”mycket bra” möte med Iran. Trump varnade i sitt tal till FN:s generalförsamling för total ödeläggelse av Iran om landet inte gör upp med USA men sa samtidigt att en sådan överenskommelse kan dröja till efter USA:s mellanårsval, vilket inte pekar mot någon omedelbar eskalering. 
Under gårdagen hann Trump även med att underteckna avtal
 om ökad militär närvaro på Grönland och att träffa Ukrainas president Zelenskyj för att diskutera en eventuell överenskommelse mellan Ukraina och Ryssland om att sluta attackera varandras energianläggningar. Världen blickar nu fram mot nästa globala höjdpunkt; toppmötet mellan Trump och Kinas president Xi i morgon torsdag. Mötet väntas inte leda till något genombrott i handelskonflikten; Kinas hot om att begränsa exporten av kritiska mineraler ger landet en stark förhandlingsposition och begränsar utrymmet för USA att via tullar pressa fram eftergifter. Att Xi inte väntas åtföljas av någon stor företagsdelegation gör det mindre sannolikt att länderna skulle offentliggöra nya stora affärsuppgörelser. I övrigt väntas diskussioner om AI stå högt på agendan. 
Rekorddyr diesel 
har fått USA:s finansminister Bessent och Trump att öppna för ett möjligt exportstopp. USA har i dagsläget ett överskott på diesel men oljeindustrin varnar för att det kommer att upphöra om administrationen helt eller delvis stoppar möjligheten att sälja till omvärlden, vilket skulle innebära en endast tillfällig prislättnad i USA men ytterligare press upp i resten av världen. 
Nasdaq lade den senaste tidens AI-oro bakom sig
 med ett nytt kursrekord för första gången sedan i juni medan breda USA-index backade något. Fed-tal med varningar för fler räntehöjningar fortsatte, från Richmond Feds Barkin (icke röstande). Stockholmsbörsen steg medan kronan – efter en volatil dag – försiktigt stärktes mot euron. Asiatiska börser är blandade; upp i Korea men ner i Kina. Japan är fortsatt helgstängt. Amerikanska och europeiska börsterminer stiger något. 
September-PMI blir dagens höjdpunkt.
 Näringslivet har varit oväntat motståndskraftigt mot konflikten i Mellanöstern och sammanlagda index för industri och tjänster ligger på expansiva nivåer i både euroområdet och USA. Frågan är vilka spår de senaste veckornas förnyade uppgång i energipriserna sätter i sentimentet och priserna. OECD släpper en konjunkturuppdatering kl. 10:00. 
Lästips: SEB:s reviderade styrränteprognoser. 
Vi sammanfattar SEB:s syn på centralbanker, långa räntor och valutor efter den senaste tidens uppgång i energipriserna och den ökade oron för mer bestående inflationseffekter. Läs mer 
här
.
Sverige
SEB:s Handlarrumsenkät: De allra flesta tror att Riksbanken låter räntan ligga stilla på 1,75% imorgon
, men en majoritet tror på åtminstone en höjning innan året är slut. Marknadsreaktionerna väntas dock bli förvånansvärt små, oavsett om Riksbanken väljer att vara tydligt hökaktiga och signalera minst en höjning fram till årsskiftet, eller om de väljer att signalera 60 procents sannolikhet för en höjning över de kommande tre mötena, i linje med SEB:s huvudscenario. Det senare skulle innebära att räntebanan hamnar långt under rådande marknadsprissättning, som i dagsläget indikerar att styrräntan ligger på 2,08 procent i december. Läs mer

articles.title: Higher near-term policy rates amid elevated energy prices and fears of second-round effects
articles.heading: Central Bank Insights
articles.fulltext:
Oil prices have remained largely above USD 100/b over the past two weeks, reigniting fears of higher and more persistent inflation. In light of recent central bank decisions, press conferences and speeches, we have revised several of our central bank forecasts over the past week. Overall, we now expect more near-term rate hikes, including from the Fed, the ECB and the Bank of England, while maintaining our view that rates will be lowered in late 2027 and in 2028.
·
Key points
Energy prices and second-round effects are in focus
Inflation data in the coming months will be crucial
If energy futures prove accurate, lower inflation in 2027–2028 will trigger rate cuts in many economies
We view some of the hikes as insurance against high inflation, aimed at containing the risk of indirect and second-round effects
We have recently revised several of our central bank forecasts. This note summarises our current view. Our latest financial forecasts are available 
here
, and our macro forecasts 
here
.
Rising energy prices are once again fuelling fears of higher inflation, both in headline measures and, through indirect and second-round effects, in core measures. Central banks face a potentially difficult trade-off: The fight against inflation has in many countries not yet been won, and policy rates that are too low risk unanchoring inflation expectations and pushing long-term yields higher. At the same time, raising rates or keeping them high for longer could prove to be a policy mistake that hurts growth and labour markets. Consumer confidence remains weak and higher energy prices and mortgage rates will hit purchasing power and may undermine so far resilient household spending in both the US and the Euro area and the hold back the recovery in other countries, such as Sweden. 
We remain inflation optimists in the sense that the current inflation dynamics differ in several respects from those in 2021 and 2022, and we expect inflation to decline in 2027–2028. We primarily expect to see the direct effects of higher energy prices, while indirect effects (through higher input costs from for instance transports) and second-round effects (on wage and price setting behaviour) are primarily upside risks. We therefore view the already delivered and expected hikes by, for example, the ECB and the Bank of England, as at least partly an insurance policy. Our forecasts balance these risks by assuming somewhat higher rates in the near term, followed by lower rates in 2027–2028 if energy prices decline.
Fed: Another hike in December
Last week’s hike was accompanied by hawkish signals in both Fed members’ projections and comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. The fact that almost all members forecast at least one more hike this year suggests that the FOMC believes one hike will not be enough and that renewed increases in energy prices are a source of concern. As before, we expect underlying inflationary pressures to continue to ease next year. In our view, this will pave the way for a rate cut at the end of 2027, followed by two further cuts in March and June 2028, bringing the target range to 3.25–3.50%. Read our comment on the 17 September decision 
here
.
ECB: Two additional hikes
The energy-price outlook has worsened significantly for the fossil fuel-dependent euro area. Our assessment of the ECB’s inflation forecasts, the press conference following its latest rate meeting, and recent speeches points to significant concerns about indirect effects. We assess the ECB’s core inflation forecast as incorporating larger indirect effects than what historical experience suggest. We now expect the ECB to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points in December 2026 and again in March 2027, taking it to a restrictive level at 3%. These hikes would be mainly pre-emptive and aimed at preventing higher energy prices from feeding into core inflation, even though there is little evidence of significant pass-through so far. If energy prices decline in late 2027 and in 2028, as indicated by futures prices, we expect rates to be lowered in 2028. Read more 
here
.
Bank of England: Energy-driven November hike to be followed by cuts in 2027
The Monetary Policy Committee is becoming increasingly concerned about second-round inflation effects from higher energy prices. If energy prices remain high, the BoE will probably feel compelled to tighten policy despite weak underlying economic fundamentals. We expect the BoE to raise rates by 25 basis points in November, with further hikes possible under an adverse energy scenario. We maintain our view that the BoE will resume its easing cycle in the second half of 2027. Read more 
here
.
Riksbank: Rate hike in sight, but not in September
Following three upside surprises, core inflation slowed more than expected in August, suggesting that the increase over the summer was partly temporary. In September, we expect the Executive Board will keep the policy rate at 1.75% while signalling a 60% probability of a hike over the following three meetings. We believe that the Board wants to wait for a firmer recovery and clearer improvement in the labour market before raising rates early next year. However, the recent increase in fuel and electricity prices, along with higher policy rates abroad, is putting the Riksbank under pressure. The widening interest-rate differential to other central banks, mainly the ECB, could become a problem for the Riksbank if the krona continues to weaken. All in all, this could prompt the Board to opt for a rate hike already this year, probably in December. Read more 
here
.
Norges Bank: Leaning towards a 24 September hike
The decision is extremely finely balanced, with markets pricing the outcome at roughly 50–50. We expect a 25-basis-point hike to 4.50%, as inflation remains too high, energy prices have risen and higher policy rate expectations abroad risk weaken the NOK. Norges Bank is likely very close to the end of its though it will maintain a tightening bias in its rate path to reflect upside inflation risks. Read more 
here
.
Bonds: Central bank expectations and broader structural forces have pushed yields higher
Bond yields have been pushed higher by a combination of central bank expectations and broader structural forces, including strong demand for capital related to AI, defence and energy investment, and shrinking central bank balance sheets. Large fiscal deficits and increasing competition for capital, including from AI-related investment, are unlikely to disappear in the foreseeable future. Higher long-term yields have reinforced concerns about fiscal sustainability, potentially triggering a vicious circle and increasing the pressures for budget consolidation measures in a situation where voters are already expressing discontent in many places. In the US, expectations for higher productivity growth from AI have also raised questions about the level of the neutral rates and the possibility of higher rates for longer, in a normalisation after the post-GFC era. As with policy rates, energy prices are key to our bond-yield forecast. We expect US and German yields to remain broadly range-bound around current levels in the near term, before edging lower as markets begin to price in cuts by the Fed and the ECB. Read more 
here
.
Currencies: Higher-yielding currencies benefit in the near term
The current environment favours countries and currencies that are perceived as safe havens, offer higher policy rates or yields, and/or benefit from commodity exposure. We believe that currency markets have largely priced in the expected Fed and ECB moves, and we expect EUR/USD to trade within a sideways range for the rest of 2026. Once energy prices decline, presumably in the beginning of next year, markets will begin to price in peak rates, which should boost euro against the dollar 2027. The SEK is likely to face headwinds this autumn and winter as the Riksbank contends with unfavourable policy-rate differentials and the currency’s usual weakness during periods of elevated global uncertainty. It will therefore probably not be until next year that the SEK strengthens, triggered when the market begins to price in the rate cuts from Fed and ECB. We also believe that policy-rate expectations for the SEK are largely priced in.

articles.title: Lower oil prices and Trump speech
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Oil prices fell back
 yesterday towards $100 (Brent) on hopes of diplomatic progress between the US and Iran in connection with today's UN meeting in New York, where Donald Trump will speak. Trump has also said that he can probably consider meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is also expected to be in New York. Larger-than-expected oil outflows from the Middle East and a recovery in oil shipping through Saudi Arabia also contributed to the oil price fall, although it rose slightly again overnight.
Yields on government bonds fell 
on a broad front yesterday, as a result of lower oil prices. The interest rate declines come after recent gains, which have reflected increased concerns about inflation, high public debt and a rising bond supply as corporate borrowing also increases. In Europe, 
in particular developments in France, where high public debt and a large budget deficit are likely to lead to large savings in the budget (just over EUR 50 billion) for next year. The interest rate differential between the 10-year French government bond yield and the German equivalent rose last week to over 100 basis points, but narrowed marginally yesterday.
The fall in oil prices and lower long-term interest rates diluted risk appetite and stock markets rose in general yesterday, driven by technology stocks (S&P500 +1.5%, Nasdaq +2.3% and Euro Stoxx 50 +1.3%). The Stockholm Stock Exchange's 
OMX 30  gained +1.3%, while government bond yields, like the rest of the world, fell back. The Swedish krona showed only small movements.
More rate hikes. 
 Chicago Fed Chair Goolsbee said yesterday that demand could drive inflation, alongside supply shocks and that the path back to 2 percent inflation will not be painless and may require faster rate hikes. Musalem, head of the Fed in St. Louis, is also on the tighter track and said yesterday that more rate hikes may be needed. Today we get several speeches from the ECB and the Fed.
Japanese markets are closed today. Other Asian stock markets are rising, while stock market futures indicate positive openings in both the US and Europe today.
The data calendar is thin
, but we get consumer confidence in the euro area, which is an important indicator of consumption. It is worth noting, however, that actual consumption developments in recent times have been somewhat stronger than indicated by weak consumer confidence. This pattern is even clearer in Sweden.
Tricky German political landscape
. Sunday's state elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin were not only a defeat for Merz's Christian Democratic party, the CDU, but also a clear indication that the political map is being redrawn. Major successes for the far-right AfD and the Left – a trend we see not only in Germany – could have repercussions for the whole of Europe, especially when it comes to support for Ukraine, energy and EU cooperation. Merz does not seem to want to resign despite the increased pressure, but wants to continue with his reform agenda in the pension, health and tax systems. His political fate will most likely depend on whether the reforms can be implemented.
Nordic key stories
The soundings for a new Swedish government continue.
 In the meantime, prosecutors are involved to investigate whether election fraud or "improper conduct in voting" with pre-crossed ballots may have occurred in Borlänge.

articles.title: Lägre oljepriser och Trumptal
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Oljepriset föll tillbaka
 igår mot 100 dollar (Brent) på förhoppningar om diplomatiska framsteg mellan USA och Iran i samband med dagens FN-möte i New York, där Donald Trump ska tala. Trump har också sagt att han förmodligen kan tänka sig att träffa Irans president Masoud Pezeshkian, som också väntas vara på plats i New York. Större oljeutflöden än väntat från Mellanöstern och en återhämtning av oljefrakt genom Saudiarabien bidrog också till oljeprisfallet även om det stigit lite igen under natten.
Räntorna på statsobligationer föll 
på bred front igår, till följd av lägre oljepris. Räntenedgångarna kommer efter senaste tidens uppgångar, som speglat ökad oro för inflation, hög offentlig skuldsättning och ett stigande obligationsutbud när även företagsupplåningen ökar. I Europa ser särskilt utvecklingen i Frankrike oroväckande ut, där hög offentlig skuldsättning och stort budgetunderskott lär leda till stora besparingar i budgeten (drygt 50 miljarder EUR) för nästa år. Räntedifferensen mellan den 10-åriga franska statsobligationsräntan och motsvarande tyska steg förra veckan till över 100 räntepunkter, men minskade marginellt under gårdagen.
Oljeprisfallet och lägre långräntor spädde på riskaptiten och börserna steg överlag igår drivet av teknikaktier (S&P500 +1,5%, Nasdaq +2,3% och Euro Stoxx 50 +1,3%). Stockholmsbörsen tog ett kliv uppåt igår (OMX 30 +1,3%), medan statsobligationsräntorna likt omvärlden föll tillbaka. Kronan uppvisade endast små rörelser.
Fler räntehöjningar. 
Chicagos Fed-chef Goolsbee sa igår att efterfrågan kan driva inflationen, vid sidan av utbudschocker och att vägen tillbaka till 2 procents inflation inte blir smärtfri och kan kräva snabbare räntehöjningar. Även Musalem, chef för Fed i St Louis, är inne på det mer åtstramande spåret och sa att igår att fler räntehöjningar kan behövas. Idag får vi flera tal från ECB och Fed.
Japanska marknader är stängda idag. Övriga asiatiska börser stiger samtidigt som börsterminerna indikerar positiva öppningar i både USA och Europa idag.
Datakalendern är tunn
 men vi får konsumentförtroende för euroområdet som är en viktig indikator för konsumtionen. Värt att notera är dock att den faktiska konsumtionsutvecklingen på senare tid varit något starkare än vad det svaga konsumentförtroendet indikerar. Det mönstret är ännu tydligare i Sverige.
Knepigt tyskt politiskt landskap
. Söndagens delstatsval i Mecklenburg-Vorpommern och Berlin blev inte bara ett nederlag för Merz kristdemokratiska parti CDU utan också en tydlig markering om att den politiska kartan håller på att ritas om. Stora framgångar för ytterhögern AfD och Vänstern – en trend vi ser inte bara i Tyskland – kan få efterverkningar för hela Europa, särskilt när det gäller stöd till Ukraina, energi och EU-samarbetet. Merz verkar inte vilja avgå trots den ökade pressen, utan vill fortsätta med sin reformagenda inom pensions-, hälso- och skattesystemet. Hans politiska öde kommer med största sannolikhet var avhängigt av huruvida reformerna går att genomföra.
Sverige
Sonderingarna för en ny regering fortsätter
. Under tiden är åklagare inkopplad för att utreda om valfusk eller ”otillbörligt verkande vid röstning” med färdigkryssade valsedlar kan ha förekommit i Borlänge.
2,9 % tillväxt i år. 
Det spår Svenskt Näringsliv i sin senaste konjunkturrapport. Lyssna på intervjun med chefsekonom Sven-Olov Daunfeldt

articles.title: Ahead of Norges Bank rate decision
articles.heading: Norway 360
articles.fulltext:
Norway 360 – Weekly Market (Re)View Norway 360 provides you with a quick and broad overview of Norwegian macro, rates and FX. 
*** See attachment for full report *** 
Macro highlights: Upcoming rate decision a 50/50 call  
Uncertainty to how Norges Bank read developments in underlying inflation drivers makes this a really close call. We are leaning towards a rate hike to 4.50% and expect the Committee to retain a tightening bias with overall small changes to the rate path. 
CPI-ATE surprised markedly on the downside 
in both Jun and Jul, being 0.6pp below Norges Bank’s trajectory. In Aug, CPI
-ATE inflation rose to 3.0% y/y, 
narrowing the gap to 0.3pp
.
 Other inflation metrics have not eased to the same extent, and other underlying inflation 
drivers 
have not changed materially. 
Inflation 
expectations have come down somewhat though business leaders’ expectations remain worrisome.
Capacity pressure is softer. 
Mainland GDP 
growth was
slightly below expectation in Q2, rising 0.3% q/q. Excl. volatile and temporary factors growth is 
broadly as envisaged by the 
Bank. Capacity utilization and labour shortages 
fell
modestly 
in 
the 
Regional network, while the labor market appears broadly stable.
Higher energy prices 
exert 
stronger external price impulses and 
lends upside risk to wage growth in the medium-term. 
This
is
also
reflected
in
a stronger NOK, with the 
i44-index 
spot level being 
1.4
% stronger than assumed.
Wage and labour market developments are broadly stable.
Read more in our Norges Bank preview: 
SEB Research
Rates highlights: Add a 2027/2028 FRA flattener to the micro steepener
September decision and rate path: We lean towards a 25bps hike to 4.50% while expecting Norges Bank to retain a tightening bias. Uncertainty is high and the risk is clearly for an unchanged rate with guidance of a possible rate hike at one of the upcoming meetings (i.e., kicking the can down the road). 
Dec26/Mar27 FRA micro steepener: We maintain our bias towards a micro steepener in the front, as we do not expect the market to price a first rate cut as early as March 2027. The curve could steepen if Norges Bank delays the next hike, which could widen the spread to 10-12bps.
Add a Jun27/Jun28 FRA flattener: The market has scaled back on rate cut expectations as visible in a less inverted 2027/2028 FRA curve. This has mainly been driven by higher energy prices and hawkish signals abroad. If Norges Bank hikes this week, we do not expect the rate path to pencil in another full rate hike. Focus will increasingly turn towards the timing and extent of rate cuts. We see scope for the NOK curve to price more cuts as inflation gradually eases. From a risk/reward perspective, we recommend adding a 2027/2028 FRA flattener to the micro steepener.
FX highlights (I): Timing NOK take profit with gas price peak – close to local seasonal high   
Europe needs to get to (peak) 75% gas storage by November to be fine this winter. Gas price bid into end of October – November a slump – then winter/Hormuz will be key. 
Even with no near-term Hormuz deal seasonally gas comes off hard from March.
FX highlights (II): The set-up in NOK argues for looking at puts in NOKSEK  
Positioning proxied by a CTA model near max long NOK – at peak of 2022. Skew higher, implied vol considerably lower than at the NOKSEK peak in 2022 – puts are interesting. The skew may in part reflect a higher carry in NOKSEK today than in 2022.  
Upcoming data and events:
Norges Bank rate decision & MPR: 
In June, both the rate path and the Committee’s guidance pointed to a next rate hike by September. Positive inflation surprises during the summer have questioned the need for further policy tightening, and the Committee softened its guidance somewhat at the interim decision in August. Inflation signals are mixed: CPI-ATE is 0.3ppt lower-than-expected, energy prices substantially higher which is also reflected in a stronger NOK, while capacity and activity data are supporting the bank’s assessment of a slightly negative output gap ahead. Overall, we are not convinced Norges Bank will argue that inflation prospects have changed materially. We acknowledge unusually high uncertainty but are leaning towards a 25bps hike to 4.50%. The rate path should maintain an upside bias though we regard the scope for further rate hikes as limited. Expectations are split and the market discounts around a 50/50 chance for a hike, with a policy rate peak of 4.64% in Q2 2027.

articles.title: Global politics and Nordic central banks in focus
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
The relief following the Fed's interest rate hike
 to safeguard confidence in the inflation target was short-lived, with long-term interest rates rising clearly on Friday. Ten-year government bond yields in most countries are now only a few basis points below last week's peaks. In France, the 10-year yield reached its highest level since 2008, while the spread against Germany widened by 6 basis points to 105 basis points.
The S&P 500 recovered
 despite the rise in interest rates and closed slightly higher (+0.2%). The reversal in oil prices, which erased an earlier increase, probably contributed to the turnaround. Despite Trump's threats of further escalation in the Middle East, oil prices continue to fall this morning. US and European equity futures are pointing higher, while most Asian stock markets are also rising. Japan is closed, so there is no cash trading in US Treasuries during Asian hours, but futures suggest that yields will fall back somewhat when Europe opens.
We can look forward to an exciting week
, especially in the Nordic region, with interest rate announcements from Norges Bank and the Riksbank on Thursday. Politics will also be in focus with the UN meeting in New York and a summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday; many meetings are planned between world leaders during the week 
and an agreement on Greenland is expected to be signed
. According to US Treasury Secretary Bessent, the US and China have started preparatory talks in a positive spirit. In a diplomatic statement, the leaders of Canada, Brazil, the EU and Kenya call on the countries of the world to increase global cooperation.
Opinions on how problematic the rising long-term interest rates
 are divided
, but I am leaning in the more pessimistic direction. It is difficult to see how highly indebted countries will be able to reverse the trend when ever higher interest costs contribute to larger deficits. Sooner or later, the market will force measures that lead to tightening and lower growth. Higher interest rates are already contributing to tightening. So far, the market can be said to be on the side of the optimists. The CDS – which reflects the market's assessment of credit risk – is at moderate and stable levels, while stable or even strong currencies for several countries with high interest rates send the same signal. At the same time, Sweden, which has the EU's lowest 10-year yield, has had a weaker currency and a shift towards safe countries, as during the euro crisis, is not discernible. Neither the central banks nor the market seem particularly worried about growth.
In Germany, the setbacks continue for Chancellor Friedrich Merz. 
 In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU looks set to fall below the five percent threshold and thus be eliminated from the state parliament, while the far-right AfD will become the largest party. The CDU is also losing big in Berlin, where the left-wing party Die Linke is making the strongest progress and will be the largest party. Despite the increased pressure, Merz is so far rejecting demands to resign.
Nordic key stories
Expectations for Norges Bank are divided
, 
but we are, with great hesitation, sticking to the interest rate being raised by 25 basis points. However, slightly lower inflation suggests that the hike can be postponed. A majority in Bloomberg's survey expect an increase, but almost half believe in an unchanged interest rate – and the undersigned is also leaning towards a later increase. More about Norges Bank 
here.
The Riksbank's interest rate announcement and Monetary Policy Report in focus
.
All analysts believe in an unchanged interest rate on Thursday and the market is only pricing in +4 basis points, but according to our interest rate survey, there are those who believe that the interest rate can be raised now in September. Our forecast that the Riksbank will wait until the labour market turns, before raising interest rates, has faced strong headwinds after interest rate hikes from both the Fed and the ECB, which were also interpreted as hawkish by the market. Perhaps even more important are the very sharp increases in fuel and electricity prices, which will push up inflation significantly in the coming months. The risks to our forecast that the interest rate path signals a clear but moderate probability of an interest rate hike in the coming months are on the upside. Unlike most other central banks, the Riksbank has emphasised that the risks of inflation should be weighed against the risk of unnecessarily harming growth. After a long period of stagnation, household consumption looks set to pick up, but the question is what will happen if households are hit by both high energy prices and higher interest rates in the coming quarters. The Riksbank cannot do anything about an energy-driven rise in inflation and, unlike in many other countries, interest rate hikes will also lead to higher CPI inflation and higher rents and tenant-owner fees. The wage negotiations, which will begin with demands from the LO in October, will hardly be made easier by preventive interest rate hikes. Di's Shadow Executive Board believes that the interest rate may remain unchanged in September, but is increasing its plans for interest rate hikes later on (more 
here
, payment link, Swedish).
Attempts to form a government have begun, 
and on Friday, not unexpectedly, Magdalena Andersson received the first of four attempts to find a government that a majority in the Riksdag can tolerate. The introduction has not been particularly optimistic, with both the Left Party (V) and the Center Party (C) sticking tightly to the red lines from the election campaign. C has even said that V must renounce the requirement to be in the government in order to even start talks. It remains to be seen how much of the proposals are negotiation tactics. Both C and V may ultimately be able to live with a pure Social Democratic government. What political concessions will be required in that case, and how C and V will be able to agree on a budget, are much more difficult questions. Magdalena Andersson will report the results of her soundings on September 28.

articles.title: Global politik och nordiska centralbanker i fokus
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Glädjen efter Feds räntehöjning 
för att säkra förtroendet för inflationsmålet blev kortvarig, och långräntorna steg tydligt i fredags. Den 10-åriga statsobligationsräntan ligger i de flesta länder i dag några räntepunkter under toppnivåerna från förra veckan. I bl a Frankrike nåddes en ny högstanivå sedan 2008 och räntespreaden mot Tyskland ökade med 6 räntepunkter till 105. S&P 500 återhämtade sig under kvällen trots ränteuppgången och stängde svagt upp (+0,2%). Att oljepriset föll tillbaka och reverserade en tidigare uppgång bidrog sannolikt till vändningen. Trots hot om upptrappning från Trump i Mellanöstern fortsätter oljepriset att falla nu på morgonen och börsterminerna i USA och Europa pekar uppåt samtidigt som de flesta börserna i Asien stiger. Japan håller stängt så det är ingen handel i den amerikanska 10-åringen men terminerna tyder på att räntorna kommer falla tillbaka lite när Europa öppnar.
Vi kan se fram emot en spännande vecka
, framför allt i Norden, med räntebesked från Norges Bank och Riksbanken på torsdag. Politiken hamnar också i fokus med FN-mötet i New York och ett toppmöte mellan Kinas president Xi Jinping och Donald Trump i Vita huset på torsdag; många möten är planerade mellan väldens ledare under veckan 
och ett avtal om Grönland förväntas bli underskrivet
. Enligt USA:s finansminister Bessent har USA och Kina inlett förberedande samtal i positiv anda. Ledarna för Kanada, Brasilien, EU och Kenya uppmanar i ett diplomatiskt utspel världens länder till ökat globalt samarbete.
Åsikterna om hur problematiska de stigande långräntorna går i sär
, där undertecknad lutar åt det mer pessimistiska hållet. Det är svårt att se hur högt skuldsatta länder ska kunna vända utvecklingen när allt högre räntekostnader bidrar till större underskott. Förr eller senare kommer marknaden tvinga fram åtgärder som leder till åtstramning och lägre tillväxt. Högre räntor bidrar redan nu till åtstramning. Marknaden får än så länge sägas stå på optimisternas sida. CDS – som speglar marknadens bedömning av kreditrisk – ligger på måttliga och stabila nivåer, medan stabila eller till och med starka valutor för flera länder med höga räntor sänder samma signal. Sverige, som har EU:s lägsta 10-årsränta, har samtidigt fått en svagare valuta och något skifte mot säkra länder, som under eurokrisen, går inte att skönja. Varken centralbankerna eller marknaden verkar heller särskilt oroade för tillväxten.
I Tyskland fortsätter motgångarna för förbundskansler Friedrich Merz. 
I Mecklenburg-Vorpommern ser CDU ut att hamna under femprocentsspärren och därmed åka ur delstatsparlamentet, samtidigt som ytterhögerpartiet AfD blir största parti. CDU tappar också stort i Berlin, där vänsterpartiet Die Linke går starkast framåt och blir största parti. Trots den ökade pressen avvisar Merz än så länge krav på att avgå.
Förväntningarna på Norges Bank är splittrade
, men vi håller, med stor tvekan, fast vid att räntan höjs med 25 räntepunkter. Lite lägre inflation talar dock för att höjningen kan senareläggas. En majoritet i Bloombergs enkät räknar med en höjning, men nästan hälften tror på oförändrad ränta – och undertecknad lutar också åt en senare höjning. Mer om Norges Bank 
här.
Sverige
Riksbankens räntebesked och Penningpolitiska rapport i fokus
.
Alla analytiker tror på oförändrad ränta på torsdag och marknaden prisar bara in +4 punkter, men enligt vår ränteenkät finns det de som tror att räntan kan höjas nu i september. Vår prognos att Riksbanken ska vänta tills arbetsmarknaden vänder, innan räntan höjs, har fått stark motvind efter räntehöjningar från både Fed och ECB, som dessutom tolkades som hökaktiga av marknaden. Kanske ännu viktigare är de mycket kraftiga prisuppgångarna på drivmedel och elektricitet, som kommer att trycka upp inflationen betydligt under de närmaste månaderna. Riskerna mot vår prognos att räntebanan signalerar en tydlig men måttlig sannolikhet för en räntehöjning under de närmaste månaderna ligger på uppsidan. Till skillnad från de flesta andra centralbanker har Riksbanken framhållit att riskerna för inflation bör vägas mot risken att i onödan skada tillväxten. Hushållens konsumtion ser efter en lång period av stagnation ut att ta fart, men frågan är vad som händer om hushållen drabbas av både höga energipriser och högre räntor under de närmaste kvartalen. Riksbanken kan inte göra något åt en energidriven inflationsuppgång och, till skillnad från i många andra länder, kommer räntehöjningar dessutom att leda till högre KPI-inflation och högre hyror och bostadsrättsavgifter. Löneförhandlingarna, som inleds med krav från LO i oktober, kommer knappast heller att bli lättare av preventiva räntehöjningar. Di:s Skuggdirektion anser att räntan kan ligga still i september men skruvar upp planerna på räntehöjningar längre fram (mer 
här
 (betallänk).
Försöken att bilda regering har påbörjats 
och i fredags fick Magdalena Andersson, inte oväntat, det första av fyra försök att hitta en regering som en majoritet i riksdagen kan tolerera. Inledningen har inte varit särskilt optimistisk, där både Vänsterpartiet (V) och Centerpartiet (C) har hållit fast hårt vid de röda linjerna från valrörelsen. C har till och med sagt att V måste avstå från kravet på att sitta i regeringen för att man ens ska inleda samtal. Återstår att se hur mycket av utspelen som är förhandlingstaktik. Både C och V kan kanske i slutändan leva med en ren S-regering. Vilka politiska eftergifter som i så fall kommer att krävas, och hur C och V ska kunna enas om en budget, är betydligt svårare frågor. Magdalena Andersson ska redovisa resultatet av sina sonderingar den 28 september.

articles.title: Major defeat for Merz
articles.heading: Euro area outlook
articles.fulltext:
The far-right AfD made strong gains in the German state elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin. At the same time, Merz’s party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), appears to have suffered heavy losses. Confidence in Merz is low, but the Chancellor has dismissed speculation about his resignation.
Key points
Major defeat for CDU in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin
The far-right AfD makes strong gains
Chancellor Merz under heavy pressure, but for now he plans to stay in office
Pressure on Merz was already high ahead of today’s state elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin, following the CDU’s major setback in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt two weeks ago (read more 
here
).
Preliminary results show that the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) appears to have lost substantial support in 
Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
, with the party only just clearing the 5% electoral threshold (13.3 per cent in 2021). The far-right AfD looks set to become the largest party, with 38% of the vote, more than double its share in 2021. The SPD, led by the popular Manuela Schwesig, the current Minister-President, is close behind with 36% of the vote.
In 
Berlin
, both the CDU and the Social Democrats have suffered significant losses, receiving around 20% and 12% of the vote respectively, compared with 28.2% and 18.4% in 2023. The big winners are The Left – after housing and rents became a key election issue – and the AfD, with 25.5% and 14.3% of the vote respectively. Overall, the AfD has made strong gains, continuing a trend seen in other state elections this year. In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD may even be able to form a government.
Difficult coalition talks
In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, it appears possible to form a government without the AfD. One option would be for the popular Minister-President Schwesig to remain in office, with her party forming a coalition with the Greens and The Left.
In Berlin, the current governing coalition of the SPD and CDU no longer has sufficient support and would need to find an additional coalition partner, most likely the Greens or The Left, in order to keep the AfD out of government. Another possibility would be SPD governing with The Lefts and The Greens.
Merz remains in office
Ahead of today’s elections, speculation had increased over Merz’s future as Germany’s leader. Dissatisfaction with both the CDU and the current governing coalition is high. However, in comments following the election results, Merz has said that he intends to continue with his reform agenda.
Our main scenario is that Merz remains in office, although growing pressure from within his own party cannot be ruled out. In that case, Merz could choose to resign himself, or some form of confidence vote could take place. However, we are not there yet.
